text:
Hello Thomas
My impression is that you get a lot less of a car for the money you spend on it. Everyone in the car industry was bragging about that the cheap Chinese cars will be more affordable... seems that there are a lot of naive guys out there to believe that. 
It's more expensive than a Tesla and it gets you less range, although you have an 82.5 kWh net capacity. To put that into perspective, the RWD Model 3 achieves 515 km WLTP with 30% less battery (LFP also), while the Seal RWD has 570 km. Then, the AWD Model 3 gets 600+ WLTP from a 75 kWh battery while the Seal gets Seal clubbed at 520 km. 
And it's not aerodynamics. Seal has a 0.219 cd value, so the extra weight and the inefficient motors makes me not bothering to consider it in the future.

Then there is the interior. Some parts feel cheap compared to something that you see on Hyundai / Kia cars, but they feel better compared to Tesla Model 3, However not as the price tag would let you believe.
The screens look best when they're turned off. Because when you turn them on, they look like the Head Units that you can buy from AliBaba or AliExpress. I was very disappointed to see that the layouts reminded me of some very cheap Chinese Head Unit that I installed on my old Honda Civic in order to get AA.
But the most obvious things were the knock-offs from other car manufacturers, that this car has: 
- the Tesla door handles
- the Bentley steering wheel
- the Leaf-like center-console with
- the Volvo gear selector and
- the 15" screen that simply has a lot of wasted space

The charging speed it nothing to write home about either. For some reason it started so slow for the first 2 minutes (under 10 kW). I thought that the charger was the culprit, but no... 
The battery charges itself in 48 minutes from 10 to 80%. To put that into perspective, my 2019 Kona 64 kWh charges in ~40 minutes in the same conditions, while having 77 kW peak power. Maybe not a very good comparison, when you look at the capacity, but with more emphasis on the time component. And my Kona has almost 5 years old tech in it.
And while it's rated at "150 kW peak", it never got more than 125 kW. The charger (300 kW EnBW) was providing 125 kW, the car showed 119 kW.

When driving, the humming at < 30 km/h was painful. I didn't got the chance to look into how can I disable it, but it was very annoying, particularly when you'd stop at a traffic light. In Hyundai / Kia, that sound is almost muted when the car comes to a halt.
Suspension was, indeed better than in Model 3, but again, you're expecting more for the extra money that you pay for it.
The car's prices are at least 3,000 € over Model 3, and you have pay an extra "surprise fee" of 1,300€ on top of that price. They call it "transfer fee".
